brief:
QUESTION: Why does revoking an enroll secret leave existing hosts running but break later
     re-enrollment?
     PROMPT: DIAGRAM: Two lanes sharing one revocation moment. Existing host holds Node key and
     continues ordinary check-ins across that moment. Installer/rebuild path holds Old enroll
     secret; a later enrollment attempt reaches a closed gate labelled Revoked. Beneath, show the
     safe rotation order as a short route: Replace distributed secret, Test fresh enrollment, Revoke
     old secret. Do not connect revocation to node-key invalidation, and do not draw a Fleet report
     that maps hosts to their enrollment secret; Fleet does not retain that mapping.
     TERMINOLOGY: Fleet is the company, product, or server. Host groups are lowercase
     fleet/fleets, including headings and labels. Do not call these groups teams. Preserve
     exact code/API identifiers. These instructions are not text to render.
     DESIGN: Flat vector technical diagram. Fleet is software for managing computers; draw no
     vehicles. Use Inter labels and Roboto Mono identifiers. At 1400 px source width use 48 px
     titles, 36 px body labels, and at least 28 px secondary text; scale proportionally. Check at
     720 px reading width and intended print size. Use a 32 px spacing grid, at least 24 px node
     padding, and consistent corner radii. Center short node names; left-align multiline
     explanations. Never shrink text to fit. Use #F9FAFC background, #192147 headings and primary
     connectors, #515774 text, #8B8FA2 secondary connectors, #C5C7D1 borders, and #D3E8F3 or #E8F1F6
     quiet fills. Use #5CABDF and #C98DEF for named categories, #3AEFC4 for labelled positive
     outcomes, #D66C7B for labelled failures, and #FAA669 for labelled cautions. Tint large panels
     to 20 to 25 percent; full strength is for small marks. Keep text navy or slate, or off-white on
     a navy anchor. Never rely on colour alone. Use one arrowhead shape, consistent stroke weights,
     box-edge termination, and labelled branches and return paths. Keep connectors clear of text. No
     gradients, shadows, decorative icons, logo, watermark, em-dashes, or slogan footer. Render only
     the specified reader-facing labels. Choose orientation to fit the relationship, not a default
     poster. Keep captions outside the artwork. If labels crowd, split the figure before shrinking
     them. Keep editable SVG when the production method supports it.
     NOTE: Proposed 2026-09-08; editorial brief, not technical re-verification. Reduce the repeated
     door/latent-failure explanation. Keep the distribution inventory, keystore differences, and
     exact rotation checklist. Keep current prose and this TODO until the actual image is reviewed.
     Then check alt text against the artwork and retain an accessible summary plus all required
     technical qualifications.
     CANDIDATE: ../../research/visual-reviews/part-3/assets/3.1-enroll-secret-rotation.webp
     Rendered and inspected for the overnight batch; awaiting final joint review.

QUESTION: How does a credential-free MSI receive real enrollment settings later?

     --enroll-secret=dummy produce one Credential-free MSI with secret-file reading enabled. Install
     inputs FLEET_URL and FLEET_SECRET feed that MSI on a host, producing secret.txt and an agent
     that reads it. The word dummy appears only on the build side, with a clear stop marker if an
     empty or dummy secret reaches the install input. Show one reusable artifact branching to two
     deployment groups with distinct placeholder secrets, never actual credentials. Do not suggest
     omitting the build-time secret is equivalent to using the sentinel.

QUESTION: How do the agent-first and Entra MDM-first Windows enrollment paths converge?
     PROMPT: DIAGRAM: Two independent enrollment lanes with the same final evidence checks.
     Agent-first: Deploy fleetd → osquery enrolls → Orbit config check-in receives registration
     instruction → Windows performs MDM enrollment. Put Windows MDM enabled, automatic enrollment
     allowed, and eligible host as a prerequisite band; do not imply Windows Server is eligible or
     skip existing-MDM/migration checks. Entra MDM-first: Entra enrollment carrying a user principal
     name → management session → no sufficiently recent agent check-in → Fleet queues fleetd install
     → agent enrolls. Put Global enroll secret required beside that install and note New agent hosts
     land Unassigned. Both lanes end at Verify agent and MDM separately, never a single
     interchangeable Enrolled badge. Omit timing promises; signed-in-user completion and the
     90-second agent-check grace belong in the adjacent text.

brief:
WHY: Equal visual spacing on clocks with different cadences suggests a shared time scale; the cooldown panel overloads the main idea.
     PROMPT: Explain the two ways an update check starts. Title: "fleetd update checks".
     Scope subtitle: "Updates enabled; default update interval". Use two compact horizontal tracks.
     Upper track, "Configuration changes": "Configuration poll" connects to "Channel change received",
     then "Orbit restarts", then a distinct event node "Immediate update check".
     Under the poll node: "30 seconds when healthy; backs off to 5 minutes after repeated errors".
     Lower track, "Existing channel": "Startup check" connects through a labelled waiting interval
     "15 minutes + up to 10 minutes of initial jitter" to "Next check", then "Every 15 minutes".
